executiveSummary: GM0703 is identity-correct and passes the deterministic ten-preset, six-checkpoint, eight-service numerical contract, but it is not a calibrated Reimerswaal first-72-hour forecast. Official 2025 data identify 23,335 residents, 28 neighbourhoods, seven BAG woonplaatsen and Veiligheidsregio Zeeland; the ten-person neighbourhood rounding difference is exactly reconciled. Reimerswaal is a long delta municipality between the Oosterschelde and Westerschelde, crossed or bounded by the Kanaal door Zuid-Beveland, Schelde-Rijnkanaal, Oesterdam, Bathse Spuikanaal, A58, N289, N659 and the Zeeland rail corridor. Nevertheless, the named Rhine/Meuse/IJssel preset assigns a persistent legacy floodDepthM value of 0.575897 through T+72 without a selected source water, defence state or connected footprint, while the coastal preset assigns zero direct depth despite unresolved estuary, primary-defence and compartment pathways. Eight unrelated active presets reuse exactly one complete 28-neighbourhood severity order. The pluvial result ignores Reimerswaal's own stress-test and sewer evidence, including 141 kilometres of gravity sewer, 39 main pumps and 302 pressure-sewer pumps in the 2021 inventory and known end-of-life pressure-pump issues. A date-bound 3 September 2026 reproduction also leaves the eastern N289 logical edge unrestricted even though Rijkswaterstaat closed the Kreekrakbrug to motor traffic from 13 July through 25 October 2026, with distinct active-mode and agricultural exceptions. Ninety-four public water-register objects, five current Waterinfo observations, Stedin/Evides provider territories, one grid-planning sample, 57 antenna sites, 18 education records, three stations and 37 transit stop areas add valuable context but do not establish connected topology, event-time state, capacity, backup, access or restoration. Unsupported local hazard, exposure, lifeline and recovery precision must be suppressed or replaced by authority-selected, versioned scenarios; missing or empty feeds remain Unknown or NoData, never safe, open or available.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: GM0703 official 2025 statistics, generalized geography, BAG woonplaatsen and neighbourhoods
evidenceSources.edition: CBS 2025; BAG/PDOK and BRT snapshots retrieved 31 August 2026
supports: Annual CC BY 4.0 CBS data identify GM0703 as Reimerswaal and report 23,335 residents, density 229 per square kilometre, 4,215 residents aged 65 or older (18.1% after rounding), and 3,199 one-person households. Official zero, rounded, suppressed, unavailable and not-applicable fields retain distinct semantics.

The municipal reference point [4.135324209374728, 51.41420369589648] is inside the 2025 generalized multipolygon. Twenty-eight neighbourhoods occur in seven districts; their published populations sum to 23,325, ten below the municipal total (-0.043%), while generated allocation reconciles exactly to 23,335.

Seven active BAG woonplaatsen are Hansweert, Krabbendijke, Kruiningen, Oostdijk, Rilland, Waarde and Yerseke. Fifteen BRT labels use separate settlement classifications. Hansweert and Yerseke BAG label points lie just outside the independently versioned generalized CBS polygon, a retained generalization/edition signal rather than evidence that the official places are foreign.

CBS resident totals omit incident-time road, rail and shipping users, pupils, patients, visitors, seasonal labour, shellfish/port workers and responders; aggregate age and household fields do not identify individual vulnerability or location during an event.

evidenceSources.title: Verbreed Gemeentelijk Rioleringsplan Reimerswaal 2022–2026
evidenceSources.edition: Final report 12 January 2022; inventory reference date 1 January 2021
supports: The municipality reports local and regional climate stress tests and risk dialogues and explicitly distinguishes intense rain, long wet periods, drought, heat and sea-level rise. It states that extreme climate effects cannot be solved by sewer or surface-water systems alone and that water-sensitive locations were mapped for phased improvement.

The 1 January 2021 inventory contains 10,623 sewer connections, about 141 kilometres of gravity sewer (77 mixed, 35 rainwater and 29 wastewater), ten peripheral facilities, 39 main sewer pumps, 302 pressure-sewer pumps and about 8,680 street drains. These are planning/inventory facts, not current connected topology, available capacity or event-time operating state.

The plan records increased failures among pressure-sewer pumps approaching expected end of life, schedules clustered replacement during the five-year plan, and identifies a completed urban-water study for Krabbendijke plus planned BRP/SWO work for Rilland, Kruiningen and possibly Yerseke. Lifecycle and completion must be verified before any protective effect is assumed.

Municipal pumps are monitored through AquaviewX and linked to Scheldestromen SCADA for coordination, but those protected operating systems and live settings are not public inputs. The public plan cannot support exact T+0–T+72 drainage, wastewater, power-backup or restoration percentages.

evidenceSources.title: Dijkversterking Hansweert
evidenceSources.edition: Project completed in 2026 and officially opened 8 May 2026
supports: Scheldestromen states that the Westerschelde primary dike from the Hansweert lock complex toward Kapellebank/Langeweg failed the newer legal assessment because height and inner-slope stability required strengthening; the authority cautioned that this did not mean an acute unsafe situation.

The 5.15–5.2 kilometre reinforcement was completed in 2026 and opened on 8 May 2026. Completion changes the applicable defence configuration, but a project page is not a live crest, damage, gate, seepage, overtopping or breach observation and is not an all-flood all-clear.

The project crosses Reimerswaal and Kapelle governance, roads, the Schore pumping system and Hansweert settlement context. Any exercise must retain the selected defence section, project lifecycle, source water, level/hydrograph, failure mode, connected footprint, arrival, persistence, probability and uncertainty.

evidenceSources.title: N289 Kreekrakbrug closure and Reimerswaal A58/Vlaketunnel corridor context
evidenceSources.edition: Notice published 8 June 2026; closure 13 July 00:00–25 October 2026 21:00
supports: Rijkswaterstaat closes the N289 Kreekrakbrug to motor road traffic during the stated interval and directs that traffic to the adjacent A58. Pedestrians and cyclists remain allowed; agricultural vehicles have three escorted weekday windows or a Bathsebrug detour, and a separate 12–19 October interval closes the bridge to all traffic.

The deployed monthly CC0 NWB snapshot represents A58 and N289 links both east to Woensdrecht and west to Kapelle, plus N659 to Tholen and N670 to Kapelle. The generalized 260/150 scenario units are logical ceilings, not measured emergency, freight, evacuation or detour throughput.

A reference-date compound reproduction for 3 September 2026 leaves eastern edge nwb-link-837-GM0703-GM0873 with no restriction state and effective capacities 103.432310 for both Mobility and Supply. The bounded NDW snapshot also has no GM0703 match; feed absence does not override the exact official notice or prove a road open.

Rijkswaterstaat describes the Vlaketunnel as the A58 crossing beneath the Kanaal door Zuid-Beveland in Reimerswaal/Kapelle, used by about 55,000 vehicles per day and monitored continuously. Static geometry and average traffic do not establish event-time tube, canal, rail, bridge, detour or emergency-priority operation.

evidenceSources.title: Oesterdam, Kreekraksluizen, Bathse Spuisluis and public water observations
evidenceSources.edition: Current RWS asset pages; Waterinfo deployment snapshot retrieved 2–3 September 2026
supports: Rijkswaterstaat describes the 10.5-kilometre Oesterdam as the compartment barrier separating tidal Oosterschelde from the Schelde-Rijn connection, with two Kreekraksluizen used by about 80,000 ships annually. RWS maintains the dam and operates the locks; current project pages describe phased 2023–2026 lock maintenance with one chamber normally retained.

The Bathse Spuisluis drains excess freshwater from Zoommeer through six culverts toward the Westerschelde, with a published design figure of 300,000 litres per second. It is a distinct water-level and water-quality control pathway, not evidence of GM0703 flood depth, present discharge, available capacity or protection from every event.

The deployed Waterinfo snapshot assigns five fresh observations near Rilland/Bath, including one point discharge and four water levels, but no forecast point to GM0703. Point observations do not form a municipal hydraulic surface or scenario forecast; a zero Bath discharge observation is not zero drainage need, and empty forecast coverage is NoData.

A governed hydraulic adapter needs a selected Oosterschelde, Westerschelde, Zoommeer, canal, defence or pluvial case with datum, valid time, footprint, depth/velocity/arrival/recession, control state, resolution, licence and NoData. These mechanisms cannot be substituted by the Rhine/Meuse/IJssel proximity screen.

evidenceSources.title: Regionaal Crisisplan Veiligheidsregio Zeeland 2026–2029
supports: The current official plan covers Reimerswaal in the northern on-call district and distinguishes acute threat, flash disaster and long-duration crisis. It names high water, extreme weather, digital attack and vital-infrastructure failure as crisis examples and provides organization, authority and escalation semantics.

The plan says Zeeland's geography means the 30-minute CoPI arrival norm cannot always be met outside focus areas. It defines notification and team start norms but does not promise resource arrival, local asset restoration, evacuation completion or essential-service recovery in GM0703 by T+72.

The plan requires current shared situational awareness, partner coordination, shelter/care, crisis communication and handoff to recovery; it also identifies a Commandoteam Water for Deltawater incidents. Strategic roles and norm times are not a live incident/action/resource ledger.

The associated regional-risk material includes sea flooding, storms, transport incidents, hazardous substances, nuclear events and societal disruption including cyber/telecom. Inclusion establishes planning scope, not the simulator's exact local magnitude, neighbourhood order or service curve.

evidenceSources.publisher: Het Waterschapshuis / Stichting Mijn Aansluiting / Netbeheer Nederland / RDI / DUO
evidenceSources.title: Public managed-water, provider, grid-planning, antenna and education context for GM0703
evidenceSources.edition: Deployment snapshots retrieved 2–3 September 2026; provider WMS queried 3 September 2026
supports: The partial CC BY-SA 4.0 HWH/PDOK aggregation assigns 94 points to the full-resolution CBS 2025 GM0703 polygon: twelve sewer pumps, two wastewater-treatment plants, eleven surface-water pumps, four sluices and 65 weirs. Seventy-one capacities are null; all twelve sewer-pump manager/status fields are null, and non-null numbers lack safe common unit, connectivity and live-state semantics.

A public-domain Mijn Aansluiting point query identifies Stedin for electricity and gas and Evides for drinking water at the municipal reference point; drainage and telecom return empty. Responsibility at one point is not municipality-wide topology, customer mapping, pressure, load, switching, backup, outage or restoration, and an empty discipline is Unknown.

One Partners in Energie sample identifies Stedin area CM44 Rilland with null existing/required withdrawal capacity, 2.5 MW and nine queued withdrawal requests, and planning projects no earlier than 2030. This is a single-postcode large-user planning sample, not live reserve, customer service or T+72 state.

RDI assigns 57 antenna sites and DUO assigns 18 education-location records within GM0703. Sites and registered uses do not establish radio coverage/backhaul/power, incident-time pupils, shelter designation, accessibility, staffing, supplies or operation.

evidenceSources.title: Public acute-care questionnaire and cross-boundary emergency-care context
evidenceSources.edition: Current Adrz page; RIVM acute-care questionnaire v1.1 published 3 July 2026
supports: RIVM's CC0 questionnaire assigns no acute-care point to GM0703. Adrz states that 24-hour acute and emergency care is available at Goes, outside Reimerswaal; its Goes hospital has a level-2 emergency/trauma profile and the region's level-2 intensive-care function.

This supports a cross-boundary care dependency, not incident-time acceptance, occupancy, staff, ambulance location, backup power, drinking water, oxygen, medicines, route passability or restoration. Access from Reimerswaal can depend on A58 and the Vlaketunnel/canal corridor.

Empty local acute-care, air-quality, seismic and weather-observation point sets in the bounded deployment are coverage facts, not zero need, pollution, shaking or weather. Current observations and facility questionnaires cannot be projected onto an arbitrary exercise clock.

identity.summary: Official code, name, province, safety region, reference point and headline statistics agree.
notes: GM0703 is uniquely Reimerswaal in Zeeland and Veiligheidsregio Zeeland.
The municipal reference point is contained in the 2025 generalized multipolygon; boundary and statistics editions are both 2025.
Annual statistics, 2021 sewer inventory, current 2026 plans/works/observations and the synthetic exercise clock remain distinct temporal claims.

geography.summary: The official multipolygon is coherent, but generalized land geometry cannot resolve estuary, defence, canal, compartment and polder hydraulics.
notes: Full-resolution geometry is needed for the Oosterschelde, Westerschelde, Kanaal door Zuid-Beveland, Schelde-Rijnkanaal, Oesterdam, Bathse Spuikanaal, primary dikes and polders.
The completed Hansweert reinforcement changes the applicable defence state but does not supply a live event or all-clear.
Hansweert and Yerseke BAG label-point mismatch is an independent-edition/generalization caveat; polygon intersection and official place identity are retained.

demography.summary: CBS 2025 headline totals agree and the small neighbourhood rounding difference is explicitly reconciled.
notes: Population 23,335, density 229, age65Pct 18.1 and one-person households 3,199 agree with the direct CBS record.
Published neighbourhood populations total 23,325 (-10); model allocation totals exactly 23,335. Published neighbourhood households total 9,560 and age65+ rows total 4,200.
Resident aggregates do not measure incident-time presence, evacuation need, disability, transport access, medicine dependence or household preparedness.

regionalDetail.summary: All 28 neighbourhoods and 36 expected fields load, but several statistics and operational infrastructure states are incomplete.
notes: District heating and public charging are null in 28/28 neighbourhoods; cars per household are null in seven, and housing/value/tenure or benefit fields in three. Null is not zero.
The 2021 municipal sewer inventory and 94 current public water-register points differ in scope, ownership, granularity and date and must not be summed into live capacity.
Provider, grid-planning, antenna and education records are static context and do not establish event-time availability.

settlements.summary: Seven active BAG woonplaatsen and fifteen BRT settlements load with source-specific membership and classification caveats.
notes: BAG place membership includes Hansweert, Krabbendijke, Kruiningen, Oostdijk, Rilland, Waarde and Yerseke; BRT additionally labels small settlements and buurtschappen under a different purpose.
The Hansweert and Yerseke label points lie just outside the generalized CBS polygon, but this is not grounds to drop either official place.
Settlement labels must not duplicate CBS resident allocation or imply visitor, worker, pupil or care-resident counts.

transport.summary: Static road, station and transit inputs are reproducible, but current Kreekrak restriction and typed crossing/rail dependencies are incomplete.
notes: Six NWB logical links represent A58, N289, N659 and N670; A58 and N289 each form one through corridor, not additive east/west capacity pools.
Three ProRail stations and 37 GTFS stop areas establish geometry/schedules, not event-time service, rolling stock, staffing, accessibility or evacuation throughput.
The active N289 Kreekrakbrug motor closure is absent even in a 2026-09-03 reference-date reproduction; exceptions and the A58/Bathsebrug detours must remain distinct.
Vlaketunnel, canal/lock/bridge, Oesterdam, rail and external-care continuity have no direction-specific valid-time operating state.

emergencyContext.summary: Responsible authorities and hazards are identifiable, but no auditable GM0703 action/resource state supports the first 72 hours.
notes: Required state includes warning, source water/defence/control decisions, evacuation/shelter, road/bridge/tunnel/rail control, pump/wastewater actions, care continuity, temporary water/sanitation, utility repair, food/fuel/medicine distribution and mutual aid.
The crisis plan defines roles and norm times, not completed actions, available crews, materials, transport, shelter capacity or restoration guarantees.
Adrz Goes is a plausible regional dependency, not guaranteed acceptance or route access; empty in-boundary acute-care records remain NoData.

scenarioMatrix.summary: All ten canonical presets return complete deterministic snapshots at six checkpoints and across eight services; realism failures are separate.
notes: The focused Vitest gate covered severe storm, pluvial flood, river flood, coastal flood, heatwave, winter storm, cyberattack, earthquake, wildfire and compound at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 for all eight services.
The UI scenario factory is a thin clone of the canonical sim-core presets; no second divergent preset implementation was found.

numericalInvariants.summary: Bounds, determinism, ledgers, monotonic cumulative burden and local reconciliation pass exactly within test tolerances.
notes: Hazard severity, system pressure, availability, route utilization and exposed population remain finite and bounded; delivery never exceeds demand.
Hazard and pressure contributions reconcile, service ledgers start from one and reconcile to availability, and counterfactual deltas reconcile.
Repeated T+24 snapshots are byte-deterministic; event-attributable person-hours are nondecreasing.
At compound T+24, every service's 28 official local regions reconcile population 23,335, affected 13,901, demand and delivered supply with error at most 1e-6.

spatialPlausibility.summary: Local hazard allocation uses broad proximity and a shared seed rather than Reimerswaal's distinct delta, drainage, settlement and source geometries.
notes: The named major-river preset retains legacy floodDepthM 0.575897 through T+72 without Rhine/Meuse/IJssel source selection, hydraulic connectivity or defence state.
Coastal direct depth is zero even though Westerschelde/Oosterschelde and defence/compartment cases remain unselected; zero is Unknown outside the narrow generated screen, not safe.

Severe storm, pluvial, river, coastal, heat, winter, cyber and wildfire have the identical complete 28-neighbourhood T+24 severity order, beginning with Verspreide huizen Waarde, Hansweert-Tramper and Rilland-Bath.
Pluvial 0.348083 legacy depth and local ranks do not sample published SWO/stress-test, terrain, sewers, polders, pumps, receiving water or control state.

serviceDependencies.summary: Road transfers are now scoped to Mobility and Supply, but exact lifeline curves remain uncalibrated and omit connected water, utility, care and crossing state.
notes: The six NWB links correctly appear only for Mobility and road-logistics Supply, with logical-proxy semantics; their scenario-unit capacities are not physical throughput.
N289 restriction, A58/Vlaketunnel, N659/Oesterdam, bridges, canal/lock and rail operations are absent from typed first-72-hour dependency state.
Ninety-four water objects and the municipal sewer inventory do not form connected catchments, flows, controls, power/backup or restoration.
Stedin/Evides territories, one grid sample, antennas and facility records do not support exact power, water, gas, telecom or care availability.

causalTrace.summary: Arithmetic attribution and counterfactuals reconcile, but causal provenance stops at scenario formulas and logical proxies.
notes: Exact-stage hazard, pressure and service effects are inspectable and deterministic.
The ledgers do not cite a selected hydraulic surface, event-valid road/crossing state, pump/utility topology, outage, crew, material, care-acceptance or restoration record.
Provider records, maintenance plans, realized asset status and current point observations remain affectsSimulation=false context; none can silently validate synthetic service decimals.

recovery72h.summary: T+72 paths are numerically coherent but have no Reimerswaal incident, action, resource or blocking-state calibration.
notes: Compound T+24, T+48 and T+72 keep system pressure 0.562832, affected population 13,901 and all eight service availabilities exactly fixed while severity falls from 0.949367 to 0.567344 to 0.510447 and person-hours climb from 250,413.652 to 954,988.229.
The persistent river curve and clearing storm/pluvial/winter/coastal/fire curves do not reference defence, pump, bridge/tunnel/road/rail, utility, shelter, care or logistics actions.
No owner, authorization, prerequisite, crew, material, fuel, water, route, start/end, completion or uncertainty supports deterioration, plateau, reopening or recovery.
Crisis-plan norm times and project completion dates cannot be converted into service restoration or a 72-hour all-clear.

findings.summary: The complete deterministic numerical and local-reconciliation contract passes.
findings.evidence: The required focused gate passed one file and two tests in 31.93 seconds. Across 10 presets × 6 checkpoints × 8 services, values are finite and bounded, delivery does not exceed demand, ledgers/counterfactuals reconcile, T+24 is deterministic and cumulative person-hours are monotonic. Compound T+24 local detail sums exactly to 23,335 residents and 13,901 affected for every service.
findings.action: Retain the coverage gate and exact reconciliation tests, but keep numerical correctness distinct from physical calibration and public-source validity.

findings.summary: The Rhine/Meuse/IJssel preset assigns persistent direct flood precision to a different delta water system.
findings.evidence: The canonical preset is explicitly named Rhine, Meuse & IJssel high water. GM0703 receives floodDepthM 0.202716 at T+6 and 0.575897 at T+12/24/48/72, with 3,498 affected at T+24 and 3,951 at T+72. RWS and Scheldestromen instead identify Oosterschelde, Westerschelde, Schelde-Rijn/Zoommeer, Bath discharge, canal, primary-defence and polder mechanisms; no source, level, defence state or connected hydraulic footprint maps the named preset to the municipality.
findings.action: Suppress the local river amplitude and consequences unless an authority-reviewed named hydraulic case provides source water, level/hydrograph/datum, defence/control state, connected footprint, depth/velocity/arrival/recession, probability, resolution, licence, valid time and NoData. Keep indirect regional supply effects separate.

findings.summary: Zero coastal depth is not a defensible all-clear for Reimerswaal's estuary, dike and compartment pathways.
findings.evidence: The coastal preset reports zero direct depth and zero affected residents at every checkpoint but still generates wind-related Mobility/Supply pressure and 26,531.482 cumulative person-hours by T+72. Official sources identify tidal Oosterschelde and Westerschelde exposure, Oesterdam/Kreekrak compartments, Bath controls and a Hansweert defence whose 2026 strengthening materially changes the applicable configuration. No surge boundary, defence section, breach/overtopping state or footprint is selected.
findings.action: Expose coastal direct impact as Unknown until an expert-selected current LIWO/Scheldestromen/RWS case is bound. Retain zero only for an explicitly scoped no-inundation scenario, distinguish wind and indirect access effects, and preserve the completed Hansweert project lifecycle without inferring live safety.

findings.summary: Eight physically unrelated active hazards reuse exactly one complete neighbourhood severity order.
findings.evidence: At T+24, severe storm, pluvial, river, coastal, heat, winter, cyber and wildfire all rank the 28 neighbourhoods identically, starting BU07030309 Verspreide huizen Waarde, BU07030501 Hansweert-Tramper and BU07030406 Rilland-Bath. The local scalar changes but the order does not. Official sources distinguish coastal/defence, urban-drainage, rural water, heat, road/rail, cyber-target and settlement mechanisms; they cannot justify one common spatial order.
findings.action: Replace the municipality seed with source- and mechanism-specific full-polygon adapters. Require cross-preset tests that unrelated hazards do not silently share a complete ranking; when compatible spatial evidence is missing, render Unknown rather than a precise ordered footprint.

findings.summary: Pluvial depth and drainage effects ignore available municipal sewer, stress-test and lifecycle evidence.
findings.evidence: At T+24 the pluvial preset reports legacy depth 0.348083, 1,978 affected and Drainage availability 0.549947. The municipal plan identifies local stress testing, water-sensitive locations, Krabbendijke SWO work, 141 km of gravity sewer, 39 main pumps, 302 pressure pumps, increased end-of-life pump failures and phased projects. HWH adds 94 partial objects. None supplies the model's catchments, rainfall-to-runoff, terrain, sewer capacity, blockage, power/backup, controls, receiving levels or current project state.
findings.action: Ingest a municipality-authorized GWSW/BRP/SWO or documented stress-test surface with feature date, rain duration/return period, CRS, resolution, licence, coverage and NoData; bind reviewed catchments, sewers, pumps, controls, receiving water, power/backup and project lifecycle. Registers remain non-causal until units/topology/state are compatible.

findings.summary: The active N289 Kreekrakbrug motor-traffic closure is absent from a matching reference-date run.
findings.evidence: RWS gives an exact 13 July 00:00–25 October 2026 21:00 motor-traffic closure, A58 detour, continuous pedestrian/cycle passage, limited escorted agricultural windows and a separate all-mode closure in October. Yet on referenceDate 2026-09-03, nwb-link-837-GM0703-GM0873 has no restriction state and retains 103.432310 effective Mobility and Supply capacity with nonzero flows. transport-restrictions.json does not contain the notice and the bounded NDW set has no local record.
findings.action: Curate the exact RWS notice against reviewed NWB Kreekrakbrug geometry and the eastern N289 corridor, retaining publisher, issue/retrieval time, valid-from/to including clock time, affected/unaffected classes, agricultural windows and detours. Because the notice is human-readable and no modal mix/throughput is published, show valid-time context and Unknown numeric effect rather than inventing total-route capacity.

findings.summary: Managed surface water, wastewater and drinking water are collapsed into unsupported service decimals.
findings.evidence: Public data provide 94 water points (12 sewer pumps, two wastewater plants, 11 surface-water pumps, four sluices and 65 weirs), five Waterinfo observations, the Bath/Oesterdam/Kreekrak system and Evides responsibility at one point. Seventy-one register capacities are null, all sewer-pump manager/status fields are null, remaining values lack safe common unit/connectivity/state semantics, and no forecast point is assigned. Exact compound T+24 Water 0.349367 and Drainage 0.264385 are therefore not operator measurements or forecasts.
findings.action: Represent drinking-water quantity/pressure/quality, wastewater collection/treatment, surface-water control and flood defence as separate typed networks. Use authorized operator topology/state where lawful; otherwise show transparent reviewed ranges/Unknown and keep HWH, Waterinfo and provider territories as evidence-classed non-causal context.

findings.summary: Exact utility and logistics availability lacks operator topology, live capacity, backup and restoration evidence.
findings.evidence: At compound T+24 availability is Power 0.328432, Water 0.349367, Drainage 0.264385, Gas 0.548818, Telecom 0.189755, Mobility 0.810195, Facilities 0.298666 and Supply 0.777443. Provider territories identify Stedin/Evides responsibility only; the Rilland grid sample has null core withdrawal fields; 57 antennas, schools and transport geometry do not establish load, switching, pressure, backhaul, priority customers, damage, crews, spares, fuel or restoration.
findings.action: Integrate authorized, security-reviewed operator outage/dependency/backup/restoration state where available. Otherwise retain municipality-level values only as explicitly synthetic ranges with uncertainty, and never convert provider areas, planning queues, antenna points, facility records or NWB roads into physical utility topology.

findings.summary: Resident-only exposure and no local acute-care node omit cross-boundary care and material moving populations.
findings.evidence: All local allocations reconcile to the 23,335 registered residents. The RIVM acute-care snapshot has no GM0703 point, while Adrz identifies 24/7 emergency care at Goes outside the municipality. CBS does not count incident-time A58/N289/rail/Schelde-Rijn users, Yerseke port and shellfish workers/visitors, agricultural/seasonal workers, pupils, patients or responders. No destination acceptance, ambulance state or route through the A58/Vlaketunnel corridor drives Facilities or Mobility.
findings.action: Keep residents as a labelled baseline and add privacy-safe, time-bounded cohorts only from governed sources or explicit exercise assumptions. Model external care as a typed destination with acceptance, staffing, backup and route state; missing live data remains Unknown rather than zero need or guaranteed access.

findings.summary: The fixed compound T+24–T+72 plateau has no incident/action/resource explanation.
findings.evidence: Compound severity falls 0.949367 → 0.567344 → 0.510447 from T+24 to T+48 to T+72, while system pressure stays 0.562832, affected population stays 13,901 and every service availability remains byte-identical. Person-hours rise from 250,413.652 to 602,700.940 to 954,988.229. No defence/control, pump, road/bridge/tunnel/rail, grid switching, telecom, care, distribution, crew, fuel, material, authorization or blocking state explains persistence or recovery.
findings.action: Require a typed checkpoint ledger for every change or plateau: authority/owner, target, prerequisite, route, crew/material/fuel/water, start/end, state, evidence time, uncertainty and completion. Do not infer action success from generic preparedness, response-delay settings, plans or elapsed time.

findings.summary: Wind, heat/drought, winter, seismic, wildfire/smoke and cyber outputs are bounded but not locally calibrated.
findings.evidence: The Groningen-earthquake preset produces a small exact 0.000343 g at T+6 without a selected event, site response or fragility model. Wildfire produces zero local flame but 0.133612 smoke at T+24 without an ignition, wind-resolved plume or air station; KNMI/RIVM local snapshot absence is not zero. Generic wind, heat, cold and cyber values reuse the shared neighbourhood order and lack event-valid weather fields, building/vegetation vulnerability, target systems, outage or authority state.
findings.action: Evidence-gate every hazard family separately. Bind KNMI issue/valid-time fields and reviewed vulnerability surfaces for weather; an event and ground-motion surface for seismic; ignition/perimeter/fuels/wind/air data for fire/smoke; and an authorized incident/target scope for cyber. Unsupported dimensions remain Unknown and numerically neutral downstream.

findings.summary: Static plans, completed projects, observations, missing matches and synthetic decimals need adjacent provenance and NoData gates.
findings.evidence: The interface can juxtapose annual CBS, a 2021 sewer inventory, a 2022–2026 plan, a completed May 2026 dike project, a current bridge closure, fresh point observations, current provider/asset registers, a level-zero provincial warning and empty municipal forecast/acute-care/air/seismic/weather/NDW matches. None alone establishes arbitrary T+0–T+72 state. Exact synthetic values risk looking observed or locally calibrated.
findings.action: Show publisher, dataset/version, issue/valid/retrieval time, coverage, licence, evidence class, affectsSimulation, uncertainty and NoData beside every value, map layer and export. Preserve project/plan lifecycle and distinguish current observation, plan, register, scenario assumption and Unknown.

corrections.summary: Correct GM0703 flood taxonomy and bind estuary, defence, compartment and polder cases only when selected.
corrections.validation: The Rhine/Meuse/IJssel preset contributes no direct GM0703 amplitude without a named connected case; coastal zero is never an all-clear. Supported Oosterschelde/Westerschelde/Zoommeer/canal/polder cases retain source water, datum, hydrograph, defence/control/project state, footprint, depth/velocity/arrival/recession, probability, resolution, issue/valid time, licence, NoData and reviewer. Indirect wind/supply effects remain separately labelled.

corrections.summary: Replace shared GM0703 neighbourhood allocation with source-aware hazard and pluvial/drainage evidence.
corrections.validation: Eight unrelated hazards cannot silently share one full 28-neighbourhood order. Versioned municipal BRP/SWO/stress-test rainfall surfaces govern pluvial results with terrain, catchments, sewers, pumps, receiving water and control state; other mechanisms use their own eligible domains and sources. HWH is a partial aggregation with contributor-dependent completeness. Realized register status is not live operation, null capacity is not zero, and non-null numbers cannot be combined without reviewed units, direction, connectivity and state.
Waterinfo's five local latest observations are points, not a municipal surface or a selected exercise boundary condition; no assigned forecast point is NoData rather than zero future water.
The Kreekrak notice is human-readable and event-updated, not a stable machine feed with modal mix or numeric throughput. Post-expiry state must be rechecked and is not guaranteed open.
NWB, ProRail and GTFS establish geometry/topology or schedules, not event-time bridge, tunnel, road, canal, rail or bus availability, emergency priority, evacuation throughput or detour capacity.
CBS residents exclude moving and temporary cohorts; public aggregates cannot identify individual vulnerability, preparedness or incident-time location.
No in-boundary acute-care point does not mean no care need. Adrz/RIVM public records do not expose live acceptance, staffing, ambulance distribution, backup or restoration.
A current level-zero warning and empty local KNMI/RIVM/NDW record sets are validity and coverage facts, not zero hazard, disruption, pollution or need and cannot calibrate arbitrary scenario time.

Nuclear/radiological and hazardous-material transport or plume incidents are regionally material but absent as explicit canonical scenarios; they must not be inferred from compound, cyber, storm or smoke output.

Exact hazard, population, service, route and person-hour outputs remain synthetic exercise results until critical/high findings are corrected and relevant authorities review the case. The audit covers only 72 hours; flood displacement, salinity, pollution, agricultural/port impacts and infrastructure recovery can last longer.
